prompt:
You are an expert SQLite analyst. Using ONLY the schema below, write one SQLite query that answers the question. Return only the SQL.
### Schema
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    Customer_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 194, 214, 256, 562, 582
    Customer_name text
    -- e.g. America Jaskolski, Ellsworth Paucek, Mrs. Hanna Willms, Dr. Diana Rath, Selena Gerhold
)
CREATE TABLE Services (
    Service_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 4, 6, 9
    Service_name text
    -- e.g. New policy application, Close a policy, Change a policy, Upgrade a policy
)
CREATE TABLE Available_Policies (
    Policy_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 246, 257, 300, 301, 346
    policy_type_code text
    -- e.g. Life Insurance, Property Insurance, Mortgage Insurance, Travel Insurance
    Customer_Phone text
    -- e.g. +16(2)5838999222, 242.763.9214, 1-416-503-7735x94204, (777)537-7792, 1-446-940-9907x257
)
CREATE TABLE Customers_Policies (
    Customer_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 214, 256, 562, 582, 641
    Policy_ID number
    -- e.g. 257, 301, 583, 346, 586
    Date_Opened time
    -- e.g. 2016-11-19, 2016-04-12, 2016-07-22, 2017-01-09, 2016-06-24
    Date_Closed time
    -- e.g. 2018-03-04, 2018-02-07, 2018-02-20, 2018-03-08, 2018-02-22
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customers(Customer_ID)
    FOREIGN KEY (Policy_ID) REFERENCES Available_Policies(Policy_ID)
)
CREATE TABLE First_Notification_of_Loss (
    FNOL_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 532, 1611, 1722, 2543, 4226
    Customer_ID number
    -- e.g. 214, 996, 892, 826, 582
    Policy_ID number
    -- e.g. 257, 993, 879, 366, 927
    Service_ID number
    -- e.g. 6, 9, 1, 4
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customers_Policies(Customer_ID)
    FOREIGN KEY (Policy_ID) REFERENCES Customers_Policies(Policy_ID)
    FOREIGN KEY (Service_ID) REFERENCES Services(Service_ID)
)
CREATE TABLE Claims (
    Claim_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 134, 145, 228, 309, 311
    FNOL_ID number
    -- e.g. 1722, 1611, 532, 2543, 4226
    Effective_Date time
    -- e.g. 1973-08-18, 2014-10-19, 1975-05-07, 1982-05-03, 1992-02-09
    FOREIGN KEY (FNOL_ID) REFERENCES First_Notification_of_Loss(FNOL_ID)
)
CREATE TABLE Settlements (
    Settlement_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 161, 176, 205, 208, 393
    Claim_ID number
    -- e.g. 717, 641, 604, 428, 360
    Effective_Date time
    -- e.g. 2009-11-20, 1971-06-29, 1978-09-09, 2003-12-28, 2006-04-19
    Settlement_Amount number
    -- e.g. 6451.65, 1588.45, 9814.39, 8827.06, 8013.95
    FOREIGN KEY (Claim_ID) REFERENCES Claims(Claim_ID)
)
### Evidence

### Question
Which policy type appears most frequently in the available policies?
### SQL
sql: SELECT policy_type_code FROM available_policies GROUP BY policy_type_code ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prompt:
You are an expert SQLite analyst. Using ONLY the schema below, write one SQLite query that answers the question. Return only the SQL.
### Schema
CREATE TABLE college (
    College_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
    Name text
    -- e.g. Saskatchewan School, B.C. School, Calgary School, Edmonton School, Toronto School
    Leader_Name text
    -- e.g. Ousame Tounkara, Ryan Thelwell, Andre Arlain, Samir Chahine, Roger Dunbrack
    College_Location text
    -- e.g. Ottawa, Minnesota, St. Francis Xavier, McGill, Western Ontario
)
CREATE TABLE member (
    Member_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
    Name text
    -- e.g. Jack Nicklaus, Billy Casper, Arnold Palmer, Tom Watson, Homero Blancas
    Country text
    -- e.g. United States, Canada
    College_ID number
    -- e.g. 1, 4, 2, 5, 3
    FOREIGN KEY (College_ID) REFERENCES college(College_ID)
)
CREATE TABLE round (
    Round_ID number
    -- e.g. 1, 2
    Member_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 4, 6, 9
    Decoration_Theme text
    -- e.g. Walk on the Moon, Soft Dream, Dark Nights, Sweetie, Summer
    Rank_in_Round number
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 4, 3
    FOREIGN KEY (Member_ID) REFERENCES member(Member_ID)
)
### Evidence

### Question
Show the most common country across members.
### SQL
sql: SELECT Country FROM member GROUP BY Country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prompt:
You are an expert SQLite analyst. Using ONLY the schema below, write one SQLite query that answers the question. Return only the SQL.
### Schema
CREATE TABLE race (
    Race_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
    Name text
    -- e.g. Rolex 24 At Daytona, Gainsco Grand Prix of Miami, Mexico City 250, Bosch Engineering 250 at VIR, RumBum.com 250
    Class text
    -- e.g. DP/GT, GT
    Date text
    -- e.g. January 26 January 27, March 29, April 19, April 27, May 17
    Track_ID text
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 4, 5, 6
    FOREIGN KEY (Track_ID) REFERENCES track(Track_ID)
)
CREATE TABLE track (
    Track_ID number PRIMARY KEY
    -- e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
    Name text
    -- e.g. Auto Club Speedway, Chicagoland Speedway, Darlington Raceway, Daytona International Speedway, Homestead-Miami Speedway
    Location text
    -- e.g. Fontana, CA, Joliet, IL, Darlington, SC, Daytona Beach, FL, Homestead, FL
    Seating number
    -- e.g. 92000.0, 75000.0, 63000.0, 168000.0, 65000.0
    Year_Opened number
    -- e.g. 1997.0, 2001.0, 1950.0, 1959.0, 1995.0
)
### Evidence

### Question
Show the name and location of track with 1 race.
### SQL
sql: SELECT T2.name ,  T2.location FROM race AS T1 JOIN track AS T2 ON T1.track_id  =  T2.track_id GROUP BY T1.track_id HAVING count(*)  =  1
